channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Greenfield names new chief financial officers
item.description: Greenfield School promotes longtime educator and finance leader Liz Smith to chief financial officer, recognizing her role in strengthening systems and guiding the school’s long-term financial sustainability.

item.title: ArtSpin brings holiday magic to downtown Saturday afternoon
item.description: Downtown Wilson transforms into a Christmas village Saturday, Dec. 13, as ArtSpin brings holiday markets, rides, Santa visits, live music, interactive arts and family-friendly fun across downtown.

item.title: Wilsonians enjoy a snowy morning
item.description: A light overnight snowfall turned Wilson into a winter postcard Tuesday, dusting rooftops and footbridges while sparing most roads and drawing families out to play.

item.title: Firefighters extinguish forklift fire at Adams Carpet One
item.description: A forklift fire at a Wilson carpet business caused $9,000 in damage. Officials say the blaze was accidental.

item.title: Commissioners finalize financing of Frederick Douglass Elementary School
item.description: Wilson County commissioners locked in financing for the new Frederick Douglass Elementary School, chose board chairman and vice chairman, renewed EMS software and set 2026 tax and meeting schedules during their December session.

item.title: 1984 murder and rape case against Parks dismissed
item.description: Prosecutors drop a 1984 murder and rape case in 13-year-old Marsha Whitted’s death after a key witness dies and DNA limits emerge, while suspect Gregory Parks remains in prison for another killing.

item.title: X marks the spot: It’s time for social media platform sovereignty
item.description: After a $140M EU fine on X, a libertarian analyst argues the future of social media may lie in platform-run microstates — like a sovereign island nation of “X” beyond Brussels’ reach.

item.title: Shortage of rural vets endangers nation’s food supply
item.description: Rural America is running out of livestock veterinarians, threatening farm viability and food safety as debt, low pay and tough conditions shrink a critical frontline workforce.

item.title: Old NC map battle helped kill latest congressional complaint
item.description: An old North Carolina redistricting fight and a 2019 Supreme Court ruling doomed the latest challenge to Republicans’ new congressional map, letting a partisan-friendly plan proceed for the state’s 2026 elections.

item.title: An open letter to the ICE agent in a mask
item.description: When federal immigration enforcement agents deployed to Charlotte, Raleigh, Durham and other places around North Carolina, terrifying and haphazard arrests ensued. Graig Meyer has some questions for the people behind the masks.
